The '''1999–2000 Scottish Premier League''' (known as the '''1999–2000 [[Bank of Scotland]] Premier League''' for sponsorship reasons) was the second season of the [[Scottish Premier League]], the top level of [[Association football|football]] in Scotland. It began in on 31 July 1999 and concluded on 21 May 2000.

[[Rangers F.C.|Rangers]], the defending champions, retained their title on 22 April 2000, after their nearest challengers [[Celtic F.C.|Celtic]] drew 1–1 with [[Hibernian F.C.|Hibernian]].<ref name="Rangers handed Scottish crown">{{cite news|url=http://news.bbc.co.uk/1/hi/sport/football/scottish_premier/722799.stm|work=[[BBC News]]|title=Rangers handed Scottish crown|date=2000-04-24|access-date=2008-04-21}}</ref>

==Teams==
A total of 10 teams competed in the league, the top 9 sides from the [[1998–99 Scottish Premier League]] and the champions of the [[1998–99 Scottish First Division]].

[[Hibernian F.C.|Hibernian]] were promoted to the league after winning the 1998–99 First Division by a 23-point margin. They replaced [[Dunfermline Athletic F.C.|Dunfermline Athletic]] who were relegated after a three-season stint in the top flight, finishing bottom of the league the previous season.

== Overview ==
The 1999–2000 Scottish Premier League was won by [[Rangers F.C.|Rangers]] for the second successive year, finishing 21 points ahead of nearest rivals [[Celtic F.C.|Celtic]]. As champions, Rangers qualified for the [[UEFA Champions League|Champions League]] while Celtic and third-placed [[Heart of Midlothian F.C.|Hearts]] qualified for the [[UEFA Cup]].

As the SPL was being expanded to 12 teams, there was going to be a three-way playoff between the team finishing bottom and the second and third placed teams in the First Division, but due to [[Falkirk F.C.|Falkirk]]'s stadium ([[Brockville Park]]) having fewer than the SPL minimum required 10,000 seats, the playoff was scrapped, bottom-placed [[Aberdeen F.C.|Aberdeen]] remained in the top flight and [[Dunfermline F.C.|Dunfermline]] were promoted automatically as the First Division runners-up.<ref name="Play-off"/> Aberdeen appeared in both the [[2000 Scottish League Cup Final|League Cup]] and [[2000 Scottish Cup Final|Scottish Cup]] final, but lost both to Celtic and Rangers, respectively. However, as Scottish Cup runners-up, they also qualified for the following season's UEFA Cup.

Celtic entered the season under new management with former [[Liverpool F.C.|Liverpool]] player [[John Barnes (footballer)|John Barnes]] taking charge in June 1999.<ref name="Dalglish back at Parkhead ">{{cite news|url=http://news.bbc.co.uk/1/hi/sport/football/scottish_premier/365579.stm|work=[[BBC News]]|title=Dalglish back at Parkhead |date=1999-06-10|access-date=2008-04-20}}</ref> It proved to be a brief and unsuccessful reign, however, after being sacked in February 2000, ten points behind Rangers in the league, and in the wake of a [[1999–2000 Scottish Cup|Scottish Cup]] defeat to First Division [[Inverness Caledonian Thistle F.C.|Inverness Caledonian Thistle]].<ref name="Barnes forced out"/>

On 20 October 1999, Aberdeen and [[Motherwell F.C.|Motherwell]] played out a match which finished in a 6–5 victory for Aberdeen at [[Fir Park]].<ref name="Motherwell 5–6 Aberdeen">{{cite news|url=https://spfl.co.uk/news/article/spl-from-the-archives-motherwell-5-6-aberdeen-2010-05-05/|publisher=[[Scottish Professional Football League]]|title=SPL from the archives: Motherwell 5-6 Aberdeen|access-date=6 February 2018}}</ref> This was the record for the highest-scoring match in Scottish Premier League history, until Motherwell and [[Hibernian F.C.|Hibernian]] played out a [[Motherwell v Hibernian (5 May 2010)|6–6 draw]] in May 2010, also at Fir Park.

Rangers secured the league title on 22 April 2000, after Celtic drew 1–1 with Hibernian at Celtic Park, leaving Celtic with a 17-point deficit with only 5 matches left to play.<ref name="Rangers handed Scottish crown"/>
